cards.text: Jesus is standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, and the crowd is pressing in on Him to hear the word of God. PRESSING in! I spent years squeezed into a junk drawer, and even I'd be looking for an exit.
Then He spots two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen have left them and are washing their nets.

cards.question: Jesus climbs into one of those two boats at the edge of the lake. Whose boat is it?
Jesus asks Simon, the fisherman who owns the boat, to take Him all the way across the lake.
Simon puts out a little from shore. Then Jesus sits down in the boat and ___ the people.

cards.text: Jesus finishes speaking. Then He turns to Simon and says, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”

cards.question: Simon is a fisherman, and his nets are already washed. What does he tell Jesus about the night they just had?

answers.text: We worked hard all night and caught nothing
We sold our whole catch before sunrise
A storm kept us on shore all night

cards.text: All night and not one fish. That's me pulling a tray out of the oven after a whole shift and finding flat, burnt NOTHING.

cards.question: Simon is worn out and his night was a bust. So why does he let the nets down anyway?

answers.text: Because deep water always has fish

cards.question: Simon lets the nets down in the deep water, and they come up empty again, just like last night.
Simon's nets are so full of fish they begin to tear. Who do they signal to come help?

answers.text: Their partners in the other boat
The sailors on a passing ship

cards.question: The partners come over, and they fill both boats so full of fish that the boats begin to ___.

cards.text: All night with nothing, and now TWO boats are going under. That's me praying for one good batch and getting so many cookies the counter starts caving in.

cards.question: Luke calls him Simon Peter here. When he sees this catch, what does he do?

answers.text: He runs to tell the crowd

cards.question: Simon Peter is down at Jesus' knees. What does he say to Jesus?

answers.text: Go away from me Lord because I'm a sinful man
Stay with us Lord and fish with us forever
Teach me Lord how to find fish like that

cards.text: Simon's companions are astonished at the catch, and so are his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. A whole crew of professional fishermen, standing knee-deep in fish with their mouths hanging OPEN.

cards.question: Simon just asked Jesus to go away from him. Jesus answers by telling Simon not to be afraid.
Then Jesus tells Simon what's ahead. From now on, what will Simon catch?
The fishermen bring their boats ashore and stay behind to sell the big catch before anything else.

cards.text: They left EVERYTHING and followed Him, right after a catch that nearly sank two boats. When I got called out of my junk drawer, all I left behind was dust and old takeout menus, and I STILL asked for a minute.

findings.problem: The question says Simon's "nets are already washed." Luke 5:2 says the fishermen "were washing their nets," so the washing is still going on. The card changes what the text shows.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats card 7's answer (all night, no fish) so a joke can follow. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke also doesn't hold together: a tray of burnt cookies isn't "NOTHING," so it doesn't match catching nothing. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment, such as Simon saying "But because You say so, I will let down the nets."
This story card only repeats card 12's answer (both boats begin to sink) so a joke can follow. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that carries the next moment.

The right answer stands out. Both wrong answers are about catching more fish ("Fish every single night" and "Twice as many fish"), while the right answer, "Men instead of fish," is a different kind of thing. A baker can pick it just because it's the odd one out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The joke calls back to Papa Dorin asking the angel for "a minute." That detail comes from his backstory and was never set up in this lesson, and onboarding only guarantees that bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The line "all I left behind was dust and old takeout menus" contradicts his backstory. He also left behind his drawer friends (the key, the batteries, the coupon), and leaving them without saying goodbye is a central part of his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. There are 7 multiple choice cards, 4 true or false cards and only 2 fill in the blank cards.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
